newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Big Malaysia trade deficit seen in April.
newsitem.headline: Big Malaysia trade deficit seen in April.

text.p: Malaysia is expected to show a trade deficit in April with big ticket import items causing the monthly trade account to show red ink for the first time since January, analysts said on Friday.
"We're expecting a big deficit in April -- in excess of one billion ringgit," said Andy Tan, General Manager of MMS International in Singapore.
"We're expecting lumpy items like aircraft purchases to be booked in April," he said.
Franklin Tan, head of research at Y.K. Fung Securities, had a similar view.
"The trade deficit is going to be two billion ringgit. This is mainly due to the import of lumpy items like the four Boeing 777s," he said.
Rajeev Malik, economist at Jardine Fleming in Singapore, had a more conservative projection.
"It will be a deficit. I've been hearing a lot of numbers, but I don't think it will be more than one billion ringgit. My estimate is between 400 to 500 million ringgit."
Malaysia recorded a 1.75 billion ringgit trade surplus in March and a 368.5 million surplus in February. The trade account showed a deficit of 102.9 million in January.
